Worked example: Harvest Lane authenticates mail.harvestlane.example in Brevo. (Mailchimp: Website → Domains → authenticate, same idea.)

RecordHostValue
Brevo code (TXT)as Brevo showsbrevo-code:… (copied from Brevo)
DKIMas Brevo showscopied from Brevo, not typed
SPF (TXT)harvestlane.examplev=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:spf.your-email-tool.example ~all
DMARC (TXT)_dmarc.harvestlane.examplev=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@harvestlane.example

Rules followed: one SPF record only, ending in ~all, never +all; DMARC starts at p=none; From address news@mail.harvestlane.example, not a Gmail address. Press Authenticate in Brevo once DNS has updated.

Send a test campaign to your Gmail, open it, then the three-dot menu → Show original:

SPF:   PASS with IP 1.2.3.4
DKIM:  'PASS' with domain mail.harvestlane.example
DMARC: 'PASS'

Submit the DNS screenshot and the Show original screenshot. If one says FAIL, check for a second SPF record or a DKIM record pasted with extra spaces.
mistakes: Adding a second SPF record instead of merging into one.
Sending the test from a @gmail.com From address, which cannot pass DMARC through the tool.
Reading the email tool's dashboard instead of Gmail's Show original.
b.pass: A Show original screenshot from Gmail showing SPF, DKIM and DMARC all as PASS for the learner's own (or permitted) domain, plus the DNS records.
b.redo: Send it back if any of the three is not PASS, there are two SPF records or +all, or the domain is not one the learner controls or has permission for.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's consent flow into Brevo, with the welcome series and 60-day win-back.

  1. Checkout: unticked box "Send me weekly prices and offers".
  2. HL·03 payment workflow, after a verified payment: IF consent → Brevo · Create or update contact with FIRSTNAME, SEGMENT, FAV_CATEGORY, LAST_ORDER_DATE, USUAL_ORDER_DAY; add to "Customers · opted in"; Supabase stores consent_at and consent_source. No consent → nothing sent to Brevo.
  3. Welcome (Brevo automation): contact added to list → email 1 → wait 3 days → email 2 → wait 4 days → email 3.
  4. Win-back: n8n updates LAST_ORDER_DATE on every order; Brevo sends the win-back when it is 60 days old and stops if they order.
  5. Unsubscribes: Brevo webhook (unsubscribed, hard bounce, spam complaint) → n8n → Supabase marketing_blocked = true, which every channel checks.

To test without waiting a week, use a copy of the automation with the waits shortened, then switch back.

Test contactSet upExpectedReceived
Ada (test inbox 1)Opts in todayWelcome 1, 2, 3All three, in order
Bayo (test inbox 2)LAST_ORDER_DATE 61 days agoWelcome, then win-backBoth
Chidi (test inbox 3)Ordered 10 days agoWelcome onlyWelcome only
Dami (no box ticked)Pays, no consentNothingNothing; not in Brevo

Then Bayo clicks unsubscribe: within minutes the Supabase row is blocked, the win-back automation stops, and the WhatsApp offer workflow skips him the same day.
mistakes: Adding every paying customer to the list whether or not they ticked the box.
Testing with one contact only, so the win-back and no-email cases are never seen.
Unsubscribes stopping email but not WhatsApp or other marketing.
Leaving shortened test waits in the live automation.
s.pass: Three or more test contacts at different order dates each received exactly the expected emails, a no-consent contact received nothing, and one unsubscribe blocked all marketing to that contact the same day.
s.redo: Send it back if any contact got a wrong or extra email, consent is not recorded, or the unsubscribe did not reach other channels.

g.answer:
Worked example: Mama Ngozi's Pantry, a fictional foodstuff shop in Enugu, with 1,240 contacts who ticked the box at checkout or on the shop's form (double opt-in). The shop moved to a paid Brevo plan, because the free plan's 300 emails a day would spread each newsletter over five days.

WeekDeliveredClicksOrders from email (UTM)UnsubscribesComplaints
Baseline: month before (no email)––0––
11,22688691 (0.08%)
21,21974450
31,231102940
41,22895731 (0.08%)

Total: 26 orders traced to email links (utm_source=email), about ₦312,000 in sales by the shop's records. Complaints stayed under 0.1% every week, so the automatic pause never fired.

Each newsletter was drafted by AI from the price sheet and approved by the owner on Telegram. Week 3's draft offered "free delivery this weekend"; the code check blocked it because it wasn't on the approved offers list, and the owner removed it.

Opens were 61% on average, but we judge by clicks and orders because automatic image loading inflates opens.

Submit: the four approved drafts, the Brevo reports, the UTM order export, the complaint and unsubscribe figures, and the owner's sign-off.
mistakes: Using a list that includes WhatsApp or phone contacts who never opted in.
Reporting open rates as the main result.
Letting the AI add discounts the owner never approved.
No baseline to compare orders against.
g.pass: Four owner-approved newsletters to a consented list, with clicks, UTM-traced orders, unsubscribes and complaints reported against a baseline, complaints under 0.1% each week.
g.redo: Send it back if complaints reached 0.1%, consent is unproven, orders cannot be traced to email links, or a newsletter went out without approval.
